quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you do?

options.text: Drive faster than the train.
Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Drive around any lowered gates.
Assume no train is coming and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs alert you that a train may be nearby. Always obey these signs. Never drive around barriers or ignore the warning.

questions.question: When should you NOT pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
When a school bus has flashing red lights.
When you are near an intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Never pass if you cannot see clearly, if an oncoming vehicle is in your way, at an intersection, near a railroad crossing, on a bridge, or in a no passing zone. Do not pass a school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road.

questions.question: Before driving after taking medicine, you should:

options.text: Ask your doctor if the medicine will affect your driving.
Have someone follow you home.
Keep your window open and drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor if the medicine will affect your driving.
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect your ability to drive safely. Always talk to your doctor or pharmacist about how a medicine may affect your driving. This is especially important for tranquilizers and sedatives.

questions.question: Which of these substances can impair your driving and lead to a DUII arrest?

options.text: Beer, wine, and liquor
Illegal drugs or prescription medicines
Inhalants like glue or paint
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving. These include alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and some legal medicines like prescriptions and over-the-counter drugs.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the accident scene.
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Stay out of traffic lanes so another vehicle does not hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a car crash?

options.text: Wear your seat belt.
Drive only on weekdays.
Stay in the right lane on highways.
Drive only between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single best thing you can do to reduce your chance of death or serious injury in a crash.

questions.question: What are blind spots?

options.text: Areas where your vision gets blurry when you are tired.
Areas next to your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors.
Traffic control devices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas next to your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see using your mirrors. When changing lanes, look over your shoulder toward the direction you want to move. Check the rear corners of your vehicle for other vehicles or objects.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights?

options.text: Drive around the gates if you do not see a train.
Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then go when the gates are raised.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then go when the gates are raised.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when you see warning signs, flashing lights, or a flagperson. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if the pedestrian waves at you.
Only if the pedestrian is not texting.
Always.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always.
questions.explanation: Always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk. You must yield the right-of-way to anyone already in the intersection. Only proceed if your path is completely clear.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol content (BAC) and reduce alcohol's effects.

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating fatty foods
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body and reduces its effects.

questions.question: When should you allow extra space between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: Your car is cold.
There are no vehicles behind you.
You are following a motorcycle.
You are listening to the radio.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are following a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Allow extra space when following a motorcycle. You need this space in case the rider falls off and you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: If you drive faster than other vehicles on a two-lane road and pass many cars, what happens?

options.text: You get to your destination much faster and safer.
You increase your chances of a crash.
You help reduce traffic jams.

questions.correctAnswerText: You increase your chances of a crash.
questions.explanation: Avoid passing vehicles on two-lane roads. Every time you pass a car, your crash risk goes up.

questions.question: What happens when drivers eat or drink while driving?

options.text: They make no driving errors.
They have trouble driving slowly.
They are better drivers because they are not hungry.
They have trouble controlling their vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have trouble controlling their vehicles.
questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These actions take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. Drivers who do this have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Four-lane traffic ahead.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that you are leaving a one-way separated highway and will soon drive on a two-way highway with traffic in both directions.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Watch for people crossing your path.
No passing zone.
Work zone ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This orange warning sign means roadwork is coming. In a work zone, watch for temporary traffic control devices and stay alert.

questions.question: What risk does fatigue increase?

options.text: Missing an exit.
Being late for an appointment.
Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue causes mistakes with speed and distance. It increases your crash risk and slows your decision-making. When fatigued, you could fall asleep behind the wheel and crash, hurting or killing yourself or others.

questions.question: When must you yield to a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog?

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading them across the street.
At all times.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes (with or without a red tip).

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver who arrives first.
The driver who arrives last.
One driver who continues without stopping.
One driver who waves others ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first.
questions.explanation: All four directions must stop at a four-way stop. The first vehicle to arrive goes first. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: When a school bus ahead has its red lights flashing on your side, what must you do?

options.text: Slow to 10 mph or less.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.
Change lanes and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: The flashing red lights and stop arm on a school bus mean it is picking up or dropping off students. You must stop and wait until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled in. Never pass a school bus that is loading or unloading students.

questions.question: What is smoking and preparing to smoke while driving?

options.text: Does not affect your driving ability.
Helps you stay alert while driving.
A distracting activity.
Not a distracting activity.

questions.correctAnswerText: A distracting activity.
questions.explanation: Smoking while driving is a dangerous distraction. It takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Left turn yield on green.
One-way.
Cattle crossing.
Two-way left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left turn yield on green.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers turning left at a green light to yield to oncoming traffic. You can complete the turn when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Emergency vehicles ahead.
Uncontrolled intersection ahead.
Four-way stop ahead.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a traffic signal is coming up.

questions.question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, what should you do?

options.text: Challenge them.
Get out of their way.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of their way.
questions.explanation: When you see an aggressive driver, the safest choice is to get out of their way. Do not compete with other drivers.

questions.question: Why is night driving more dangerous?

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the road at night.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you can only see as far as your headlights shine. This makes it difficult to judge how far away other vehicles are and how fast they are going.

questions.question: What is a crosswalk?

options.text: Another name for a four-way intersection.
An area marked for construction workers.
An area where pedestrians can cross the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: An area where pedestrians can cross the road.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks are marked with white lines to show where pedestrians should cross. Some crosswalks have no markings.

questions.question: If the road is wet or icy, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down.
Drive at the posted speed.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: On wet or icy roads, your tires do not grip well. You should slow down to stay safe.

questions.question: When are seat belts most effective?

options.text: Only for the driver.
For passengers on long drives.
For everyone on expressways.
For everyone every time you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: For everyone every time you drive.
questions.explanation: Everyone in your car should wear a seat belt every time you drive. In a crash, a person without a seat belt becomes a flying object and can hurt others in the car.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Signal the lane change.
Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal early, check your mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: If you become drowsy while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Try to fight it.
Take a break.
Take caffeine pills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a break.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired, stop at a rest area. Take a nap, stretch, or let someone else drive. Caffeine pills are not a safe substitute for sleep.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down or stop.
Stop if needed.
You must come to a complete stop.
Drive carefully and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign means stop. Come to a complete stop and make sure the way is clear before proceeding.

questions.question: On a slippery road, you should keep a following distance that is:

options.text: The same as normal.
Farther from the car ahead than normal.
Closer to the car ahead than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther from the car ahead than normal.
questions.explanation: On a slippery road, your car needs more distance to stop. Always keep a longer distance between your car and the car ahead on slippery roads.

questions.question: You see a stopped school bus with flashing lights and an extended signal arm. You should:

options.text: Stop.
Go 15 mph if no children are outside.
Drive at normal speed but watch for children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: You must stop completely. Stay stopped until the signal arm goes back and the bus starts moving. This law applies whether you are behind the bus or coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: A driver ahead is driving with one hand and talking to a passenger. You should:

options.text: Give that vehicle extra space.
Know the driver is not paying full attention and is less safe.
Not copy that driver's behavior.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving. If another driver looks distracted, give them extra space because accidents are more likely.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:

options.text: Vehicles in the roundabout.
Bicyclists in the roundabout.
Pedestrians in the roundabout.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to all pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, you should:

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and roll down your window.
Get your documents ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
Get out and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel and tell passengers to keep their hands visible. Stay in your car unless the officer tells you to get out. Only get your documents when the officer asks.

questions.question: Is it permitted to drive if medication impairs your driving?

options.text: No, never.
Yes, if you don't feel drowsy.
Yes, if a doctor prescribed it.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive if any substance impairs your driving. This includes alcohol, prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you. You should:

options.text: Stop where you are.
Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: Move to the right side of the road and stop to let the emergency vehicle pass. If you are in heavy traffic, drive slowly until you can safely move out of the way.

questions.question: You are on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle signal. You should:

options.text: Ignore it if other lanes are open for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as possible.
Slow down, move to clear a path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to clear a path, and stop.
questions.explanation: Slow down and make room for the emergency vehicle to pass. Then stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn.
Flagger ahead.
Two-way left turn.
Turn right or go straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn.
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers what they can and cannot do. It means left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: A school bus ahead has red flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop and drive when you think all children have left the bus.
Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully.
Stop and wait until the red lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the red lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has red flashing lights, you must stop and stay stopped until the lights stop. If the bus is on the other side of a divided highway, you do not have to stop.

questions.question: You see animals standing near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and drive with caution.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive with caution.
questions.explanation: Slow down and drive with caution when you see animals near the road. They may suddenly run or change direction. Some animals travel in groups, so more animals may be nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a prescription drug and drink alcohol?

options.text: There will likely be no effect.
It will make you more alert.
It can make you unfit to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can make you unfit to drive.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect your ability to drive. They are especially dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: You have an argument and feel angry. What should you do before driving?

options.text: Play loud music so you won't think about the argument.
Take a few minutes to calm down.
Drive on the interstate to relieve stress.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions affect your driving ability. If you are angry, excited, scared, worried, or sad, wait until you feel calm before driving. You need to focus on the road, not on what upset you.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Turn on your headlights.
Reduce your speed.
Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Look in your rearview and side mirrors before changing lanes. Also look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: A driver entering traffic from a driveway or private road should:

options.text: Has the right-of-way.
Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: Yield to drivers already on the public road when entering from a driveway or private road. Merge safely when you can do so.

questions.question: You pass your exit on the interstate. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn if you pass your exit. Continue to the next exit instead.

questions.question: Which statement is true about railroad crossings?

options.text: You should use cruise control near a railroad crossing to keep your speed steady.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal. Drive carefully near railroad tracks.

questions.question: A driver should watch:

options.text: Only straight ahead.
Only the center of the road.
The sides, ahead, and behind their car.

questions.correctAnswerText: The sides, ahead, and behind their car.
questions.explanation: Watch all around your car — the sides, ahead, and behind. A good driver knows what is happening in all directions.

questions.question: You see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Continue ahead. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
Pull right and drive around the pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Wait until they have crossed and the intersection is clear before driving.

questions.question: When an aggressive driver is near you, you should:

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Tailgate them to retaliate.
Make sure they know you disapprove of their behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm if another driver is being aggressive. Slow down and let them pass. Put distance between your car and theirs. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.
